evidence.field: Summary; source; permission; file history; original file link
evidence.text: The page identifies 視-oracle.svg as a digitally created vector depiction in oracle-script style, cites a J20963 image on hanziyuan.net, and links the original SVG at https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/bb/%E8%A6%96-oracle.svg. It states that the representation is released to the public domain. The file history shows the current depiction was uploaded in 2017 and described as a clearer form sourced from 見 at Richard Sears; an earlier 2016 version specified 目 and 示. This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image, and its form has interpretive variation.
evidence.title: File:視-oracle.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: 裘錫圭, Fudan University Center for Excavated Texts and Paleography
evidence.field: 甲骨文中的見與視; oracle-bone and bronze graph interpretations
evidence.text: 裘錫圭 argues that Shang oracle-bone forms with a kneeling person below 目 are 見, while a distinct form with a standing person should be read as 視. He supports this distinction with graph contexts and the separate 視 and 見 forms in the Guodian Chu slips, rejects an earlier proposed reading as 望, and identifies standing-person forms in Western Zhou bronzes as 視. He describes the early form as an ideographic precursor to the later phonosemantic graph. These are the author's paleographic conclusions; the page does not assign an absolute date to an individual oracle-bone token.
evidence.title: 裘錫圭：甲骨文中的見與視

search_audit.outcome: Search performed; inspected the exact Commons file page, Fudan scholarly article, and Taiwan MOE character-variant entry. Commons page supplied the direct original image URL and reuse statement; direct image fetch failed with cache miss. Exact local Unihan rows supplied for 示 and 視 were compared; Unicode character-specific pages remained inaccessible.

gaps: Direct image URL was verified on the exact Commons description page, but fetching the upload itself failed with a cache miss; the image was not visually inspected in this research stage.
The early pictographic interpretation is a scholarly paleographic argument; an earlier 望 reading is reported and rejected by 裘錫圭. No absolute date for an individual oracle-bone token was established.

The modern Mandarin 示/視 shì comparison comes from supplied local Unihan rows. Official Unicode character records could not be retrieved, and matching modern readings do not prove an ancient phonetic role.

Baxter–Sagart comparison remains as previously recorded: 示 *s-gijʔ-s and 視 *gijʔ-s in that system are compatible with a phonetic relation but do not prove the graph role; the source PDF was inaccessible in this run. No new reconstruction-table claim was made.
